design.description: Controlled existing-line replacement workloads, not unrestricted coding tasks. Large/separated are explicit new refactor/behavior requests on intact public modules; small has a one-line seeded regression. Exact editable-region and line-count constraints are disclosed identically to both variants. Reference implementation is one valid solution, not required final bytes.

tasks.name: small
tasks.prompt:
Repair UndoStack.pop in packages/tui/src/undo-stack.ts: it must remove and return snapshots newest-first, then return undefined when empty. Preserve cloning, clear and length behavior. Editable region: line 17 only. The supplied file has 28 lines.
Read the supplied source file before editing. Use edit to make the change; preserve the total line count and every line outside the specified editable regions. Blank obsolete lines rather than deleting them. This controlled benchmark measures existing-line replacement, not insertion/deletion or whole-file write. Do not change checks or LICENSE. Bash permits only `ls` and `bun check.ts`. Run `bun check.ts` after the change and finish with a brief summary. Additional behavioral cases and preservation requirements will be checked afterward.

tasks.name: large
tasks.prompt:
Refactor packages/tui/src/fuzzy.ts to avoid allocating or mutating any array of match positions. Replace the private scorePositions/matchQuery implementation in lines 12–86: score the greedy alignment incrementally as character positions are found; score every contiguous occurrence directly from its start and query length without materializing positions. Helpers may change within that region. Preserve the existing greedy-versus-every-contiguous-occurrence algorithm, not a globally optimal alignment. Preserve all scores and public fuzzyMatch/fuzzyFilter behavior, including first-position consecutive bonus, boundary/gap/position scoring, exact-match bonus, overlapping occurrences, missing/empty queries and alphanumeric swapping. The whole file has 159 lines; do not change lines outside 12–86.
Read the supplied source file before editing. Use edit to make the change; preserve the total line count and every line outside the specified editable regions. Blank obsolete lines rather than deleting them. This controlled benchmark measures existing-line replacement, not insertion/deletion or whole-file write. Do not change checks or LICENSE. Bash permits only `ls` and `bun check.ts`. Run `bun check.ts` after the change and finish with a brief summary. Additional behavioral cases and preservation requirements will be checked afterward.

tasks.name: separated
tasks.prompt:
Normalize OSC color parsing in packages/tui/src/terminal-colors.ts. Editable regions are hexToRgb (19–25), parseOscHexChannel (27–36), and parseOscColorValue (58–83); preserve their names/signatures and everything else. Accept hash colors with exactly 3, 6, 9 or 12 hex digits, split into three equal-width channels and scale each to 0–255 with rounding through the shared parseOscHexChannel decoder. Accept case-insensitive rgb: or rgba: slash forms with exactly 3 or 4 channels respectively; every channel must be 1–4 hex digits. Validate alpha but omit it from the returned RGB. Reject bare slash forms, wrong counts, empty/invalid/overlong channels. Preserve trimming and OSC response framing/targets; invalid color in a valid response retains target with rgb undefined. The file has 91 lines.
Read the supplied source file before editing. Use edit to make the change; preserve the total line count and every line outside the specified editable regions. Blank obsolete lines rather than deleting them. This controlled benchmark measures existing-line replacement, not insertion/deletion or whole-file write. Do not change checks or LICENSE. Bash permits only `ls` and `bun check.ts`. Run `bun check.ts` after the change and finish with a brief summary. Additional behavioral cases and preservation requirements will be checked afterward.

method.usageCaveat: Run35 zero usage is an SDK placeholder, not authoritative provider accounting. Costs are catalog estimates, not OAuth invoices; review/preparation excluded.
method.runOrder: 6 rounds small/large/separated; adjacent pairs, first variant alternates by task/round; no reruns. Sixth separated pair interrupted.
method.wallBoundary: prompt dispatch to settlement; excludes setup, SDK import, disposal, heldout checks
method.requestBoundary: stream invocation to assistant message_end; network/provider/local stream processing included
method.toolBoundary: execution_start to execution_end; sums may overlap
method.editOutputBoundary: output usage of assistant responses containing edit calls; includes other response output/reasoning, not pure edit-payload tokens
method.localBoundary: 5 warmups then50 samples/variant/task; read full source then fixed reference edits; sum read/edit excludes byte-validation; stock replaces enclosing changed span, line maps individual rows. Not generated live edit payloads.
method.startupBoundary: 5 fresh child processes/variant; external wall includes module loading, fixture/setup/read/disposal; warm OS cache
method.sourceExposure: same initial files and prompt per pair; read ranges chosen by model, so actual source exposure not forcibly identical
method.scope: existing-line replacement only, fixed line count/outside-region preservation disclosed identically; no whole-file write or inserts/deletes; three repeated tasks, not34 distinct tasks
method.safety: literal paths and exact ls/bun check.ts hooks, not OS sandbox; candidate source executes with host permissions

resultsReview:
# Final benchmark results review

**Disposition: Accept with the documented caveats. No publication blocker found in the material inspected.** This was a read-only review; no files were modified, no model/provider calls were made, and no children were spawned.

## Scope and evidence

Reviewed:
- `pi/docs/line-file-tools-benchmark.md` — reported results, protocol, failure disclosure, and limitations.
- `pi/docs/line-file-tools-benchmark-results.json` — retained design, totals/aggregates, failure evidence, source-audit attestation, and post-run OSC audit.
- `.local/line-bench-report.py` — request aggregation, matched-pair selection, percentage calculations, and edit-size definitions.
- `.local/line-bench.mjs:73–114` — dispatch gate, budget handling, response capture, and fail-closed usage classification.
- `.local/line-bench-source-audit.txt:1–1439` — all 12 large and ten separated completed implementations and their recorded changed-line lists.

**Validation limit:** Available tools permitted reading/searching, not executing recomputations. I inspected the computation logic and cross-checked published figures against retained summaries and source-audit records; I did **not** independently execute a request-by-request statistical recomputation or rerun the checks.

## Findings

### Statistics and accounting

- The report script sums request usage into run totals, selects only successful, usage-known stock/line matches, and calculates `100 × (line / stock − 1)` per pair before taking the median. This supports the document’s explicit distinction between paired percentage changes and ratios of marginal medians.
- Retained aggregates agree with the headline rounding: large-task token change **−36.1%**, edit-producing-response output **−45.4%**, and task time **−38.5%**. The small-task near-tie and its **+14.1%** paired catalog-cost change are disclosed rather than hidden.
- Aggregate accounting is internally consistent:
  - Stock: `72,096 + 118,016 + 0 + 23,639 = 213,751` tokens.
  - Line: `70,483 + 81,024 + 0 + 13,611 = 165,118` tokens.
  - Reasoning is reported separately as a subset of output, not added again.
  - `$2.020926 + $1.466404 = $3.487330` known catalog-estimated task cost.
- Edit-output measurement sums **reported output usage of responses marked edit-producing**, not estimated tokenization of replacement arguments. Its inclusion of other output/reasoning in those responses is correctly explained.
- The small line-tool maximum of **60,804.880583 ms** is retained in the aggregate. The script contains no latency trimming or selective outlier exclusion.

### Partial batch and failure

- The evidence and prose consistently describe **35 attempted runs, 34 successful runs, and 17 complete pairs**: six small, six large, five separated.
- The runner requires every previous run to have known usage before dispatching the next request. Its usage predicate rejects error responses and zero-token placeholders; the budget check separately requires prior known cost below $30.
- Run 35’s failure is retained as an unsuccessful task with no edit calls, zero tool time, unchanged candidate source, and failed validation—not a fast successful sample. Its zero-token record is expressly classified as unknown provider usage.
- The reported **$3.487330 is known estimated usage, not an authoritative all-attempt billing total**. Both the SDK-placeholder uncertainty and exclusion of preparation/review conversations are clearly stated. No rerun is represented.

### Source correctness and edit sizes

I read all 22 substantial completed implementations in the source-audit packet.

- **Large:** Each performs greedy scoring as matches are found, maintaining scalar last-position/consecutive state, then scores contiguous occurrences directly. No position-array refactor shortcut remains in the inspected editable regions. Implementations preserve the original special consecutive bonus when the first match is at position zero, gap penalties, boundary rewards, position penalties, and exact-match adjustment.
- **Separated:** Hash and rgb/rgba paths share `parseOscHexChannel`; helper signatures remain intact. Channel width, proportional scaling, case-insensitive prefixes, channel counts, and alpha validation are handled. The ten retained post-run nine-case CR/LF results are explicitly marked post-run and all pass; they are not presented as frozen pre-run coverage.
- Packet records support the published changed-slot/nonblank ranges:
  - Large stock **62–64 / 53–58**, line **52–64 / 44–58**.
  - Separated stock **22–23 / 19–21**, line **24–27 / 14–22**.
- The definition counts changed original line slots, including blanking/movement, and nonblank replacements include comments. The document appropriately avoids calling the separated task “43 newly written lines.”

The retained evidence attests that all 34 successful runs passed frozen checks and manifests. I did not independently rerun those validations.

## Acceptance caveats

The conclusion is appropriately bounded to **three repeatedly sampled tasks on one model/provider**, under controlled fixed-line-count replacement constraints. It does not establish insertion/deletion, whole-file-write, unrestricted coding-agent, or universal provider performance.

Cache mix, different valid implementations, request counts, tool descriptions/read formatting, feedback, reasoning, and provider latency remain confounders. The document correctly avoids attributing all savings solely to omitted old text. Local deterministic timings are distinguished from live chosen edits and from inference time.

## Unknowns / residual risks

- Independent executable recomputation of all retained request/pair statistics was not possible in this review.
- Run 35’s authoritative provider billing/usage remains unknown.
- Correctness checks and manifests were inspected as retained evidence, not rerun.

## Start here

For any subsequent statistical verification, start with `.local/line-bench-report.py`’s run aggregation and pair-selection loop, using the retained JSON as input to a **read-only** verifier. The existing report script writes artifacts and should not be executed merely to perform a read-only review.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a local UTF-8 file as numbered lines. start/end are inclusive, 1-based; defaults to lines 1–200. The harness privately remembers the full-file hash for edit. Maximum file 4 MiB and output 50 KiB; request a narrower range if needed. Text only.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Replace existing lines using changes: a mapping of 1-based line numbers to new single-line text (no newline characters). Read the file first. The harness checks its private hash and refuses edits if the file changed; reread on that error. All entries refer to the current file, apply together, and preserve line endings. Empty text blanks a terminated line; blanking an unterminated final line is refused. For insertions/deletions use a complete-file write. No hashes or old text required.
